item.title: Three Truths About the End of New START and What It Means for Strategic Competition
item.description: The expiration of New START does not necessarily foretell an arms race or a massive U.S. nuclear buildup. Instead, the expiration of the treaty may be an opportunity for a new era of arms control.

item.title: Sand Leaking Out of the Bag: Eroding American Influence
item.description: This week, Bill Reinsch examines how U.S. partners have looked beyond the United States to diversify their trading relationships and reduce their holdings of U.S. bonds.

item.title: The New Frontline: Technology Is a Modern Warfighting Domain
item.description: The United States must recognize science and technology as a warfighting domain and adopt technology maneuver as a warfighting concept to win the future. Discover how frontline units and tech centers across the nation must adapt now to stay ahead.

item.title: China Relocates PMZ Structure to Weihai Shipyard
item.description: The Atlantic Amsterdam, a Chinese platform that was a point of tension between South Korea and China due to its unilateral placement by Beijing in the Provisional Measures Zone (PMZ), arrived at a commercial shipyard in China last week.

item.title: Why Golden Dome for America: The Case the Administration Should Make
item.description: One year after announcing Golden Dome for America, the administration still hasn't made the case for homeland missile defense, even though the arguments are strong.

item.title: Eyes on the Prize: CCG Patrols Prioritize Scarborough in 2025
item.description: China Coast Guard patrols are evolving.

item.title: Why the Army Needs Deception Groups
item.description: To outsmart modern threats, the U.S. Army must bring back “ghost armies”—dedicated deception units that manipulate what the enemy sees and believes, creating the space and confusion needed to maneuver and win on today’s transparent battlefield.
